positions.name: GE Vernova
positions.thesis: NRC construction permit for GEV/Hitachi's new reactor design (Sep 29-30) is a concrete regulatory milestone that validates the nuclear growth story, whose coverage share jumped to 49% from 9%. With no earnings next week and only 1.1% gain last week, the news is not fully priced; GLJ's Sell is opinion, not information.

positions.name: Micron Technology
positions.thesis: Micron's Sep 30 Q4 beat with above-Street guidance on AI memory demand confirms the bull case, and the AI memory rally story's coverage share is rising (37% vs 29% avg) with a new AI Memory Boom narrative accelerating. Post-earnings drift should favor MU next week, though Burry's puts and bubble fears cap conviction.

positions.name: Netflix
positions.thesis: Deutsche Bank's Sep 29 upgrade to Buy is a new story now 40% of coverage, and the selloff-debate narrative is fading, suggesting a near-term bounce. But the upgrade came with a lowered target and weak engagement trends persist, capping conviction.

positions.name: Berkshire Hathaway
positions.thesis: Buffett's chairman exit and Howard's appointment add governance uncertainty, while the positive Abel/Alphabet narrative fades. Lennar stake increase is too small to offset. Expect slight underperformance next week.

positions.name: Lululemon Athletica
positions.thesis: Fresh Sep 30 cash-flow skepticism and Sep 25 CEO/bylaw governance changes add to negative sentiment from Sep 3 guidance cut. With no earnings next week, LULU likely underperforms as the market questions cash durability and leadership transition.

positions.name: Constellation Brands
positions.thesis: New earnings story dominates: Q2 on Oct 6 expected EPS decline, negative ESP, and analyst target cuts. Selloff/outlook stories fading, but stock already down 12.8% in a month, so edge is modest. Binary event warrants lower confidence.

positions.name: Boeing
positions.thesis: A cluster of material wins: the $20B Navy F/A-XX award (Oct 1), a $14.7B Lockheed PAC-3 seeker contract (Oct 6), FAA clearing the 737 MAX software glitch (Oct 2), and the SPEEA deal averting a strike (Oct 1). With BA down 8.8% on the month and 25% below its high, these catalysts are not yet priced.

positions.name: Constellation Energy
positions.thesis: Google's 20-year nuclear PPA (Oct 6) and Amazon deal (Oct 1) validate CEG's AI power demand, but the +18% week already prices much of it. Expect modest relative outperformance as analysts digest the contract, not a repeat surge.

positions.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
positions.thesis: Google's new 20-year nuclear power deal and Gemini 4 Argon launch strengthen its AI infrastructure and product position, while its Anthropic stake offers upside. These recent catalysts should support relative outperformance next week, though AI capex bubble fears and EU regulatory appeals cap gains.

positions.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise
positions.thesis: HPE's Sep 30 $1.2B Vultr AMD order and raised FY27 networking guidance are material positives, reinforced by Oct 1 analyst PT hikes and Oct 7 Mizuho/AMD server news. But the stock is already at a 52-week high after a +12.8% week, so much is priced; expect modest relative outperformance, not another surge.

positions.name: Lumentum
positions.thesis: AI optics rally narrative is new and rising (42% share) on Nvidia CPO demand acceleration and potential US curbs on Chinese transceivers, supporting relative upside. But +14% week and near 52-week high price much in; no earnings next week. Expect moderate outperformance, not explosive.

positions.name: Lilly (Eli)
positions.thesis: Net-positive news flow: FDA expanded Jaypirca label (Oct 2), Gate Bioscience deal up to $870M (Oct 5), and Foundayo/retatrutide data reinforce GLP-1 leadership vs Novo. Foghorn cancer-deal termination is minor and mostly hits Foghorn. Stock already up 2.7% on the week, so the edge is modest.

positions.name: Marvell Technology
positions.thesis: Oct 6 investor day raised FY28 revenue to $20B above consensus and set a $70-90B FY31 target, triggering a 7% jump and multiple PT hikes (Piper/BofA to $400). The new AI expansion story is now 61% of coverage. Positive news diffusion likely continues next week, though valuation debate caps upside.

positions.name: Nvidia
positions.thesis: Nvidia's $150B buyback (Sep 28) and fresh SpaceX $40B chip purchase (Oct 6) reinforce AI demand, while Micron's Q4 beat confirms memory/AI strength. China chip-sale easing adds upside. With no earnings next week, these active positive events should drive relative outperformance, though much is near the price.

positions.name: Nvidia
positions.thesis: Nvidia's $150B buyback (Sep 28) and fresh SpaceX $40B chip purchase (Oct 6) reinforce AI demand, while Micron's Q4 beat confirms memory/AI strength. China chip-sale easing adds upside. With no earnings next week, these active positive events should drive relative outperformance, though much is near the price.

positions.name: Berkshire Hathaway
positions.thesis: New subsidiary story [9] surges to 22% share, led by Texas AG civil investigative demands into Fruit of the Loom (Oct 07) over toxic chemicals—a fresh regulatory risk. Combined with skepticism over Abel's Lennar buying (Oct 06), slight negative for BRK.B next week.

positions.name: Lululemon Athletica
positions.thesis: Burry sold LULU for tax-loss harvesting and swapped to Deckers (Oct 6), a negative flow signal. Oct 7 leadership overhaul adds uncertainty; stock at 52-week low with no earnings catalyst. Valuation debate fading. Expect underperformance next week.

positions.name: McDonald's
positions.thesis: New AI pricing antitrust lawsuit (Oct 5-7) adds legal overhang to MCD's already weak sentiment. Franchisee pushback on $8.5B overhaul and analyst skepticism on strategy update suggest continued underperformance next week. Stock is oversold but negative news is fresh.

positions.name: Meta Platforms
positions.thesis: Muse's 27% run has priced in the AI-agent upside (story share fading 28%->19%), while two negative overhangs are rising: New Mexico seeks up to $40B with a ruling due this month, and Ofcom opened a UK probe Oct 6. Capex-debt worries (Meta owes $22B more than it holds) add pressure. Risk skewed down near-term.

positions.name: Nike, Inc.
positions.thesis: Nike's Q1 revenue miss and weak FY27 guidance (Oct 1) triggered analyst downgrades and PT cuts, with China reset and turnaround doubts persisting. Despite a 12-year low, negative news flow and rising 'stock collapse' coverage suggest NKE underperforms peers next week.

positions.name: PepsiCo
positions.thesis: News flow stays negative into the Oct 8 Q3 print: RBC sees a 'soft' September quarter, Barclays/UBS/RBC/Wells Fargo all cut targets, and two downgrades hit in two days. Wall Street is explicitly favoring KO over PEP. India label-ban suit adds regulatory noise. Earnings sits outside the holding week, so the edge is modest and largely sentiment-driven.

positions.name: PepsiCo

positions.name: Sandisk
positions.thesis: Bullish coverage is crowded price-target chatter (Surge story 34% share, Mizuho $2050, $175 target reset), not new information. Genuine news is negative: Toshiba doubling HDD output (Oct 1) and SK Hynix earnings caution (Oct 6) pressure memory-pricing sentiment. Stock already down 1w/1m and 27% off high; expect relative weakness.
